module purpose: neorv32_cpu_frontend controls instruction fetch requests from a restartable program counter and privilege state, writes acknowledged instruction-bus response halves into a two-lane prefetch buffer, and issues valid/fault/compression-qualified instructions on frontend_o, optionally using the decompressor when RVC_EN is enabled.

use-case flows.value: restart fetching from ctrl_i.pc_nxt with ctrl_i.cpu_priv, clear the prefetch buffer, and seed instruction alignment
issue an instruction-bus request at fetch.pc with current privilege/debug/fence and, on acknowledge, advance fetch.pc
capture acknowledged bus-response halves and error bits into the prefetch buffer

select buffered halfword(s), optionally decompress a 16-bit instruction, and consume one or two buffer entries on ctrl_i.if_ack while driving frontend_o.valid, frontend_o.instr, frontend_o.compr, and frontend_o.fault
frontend_o.halted when a request is blocked because the prefetch buffer is not fully free
fetch sequencing state, restart flag, fetch PC, fetch privilege, and issue alignment forced to reset values while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: fetch.pc is loaded from ctrl_i.pc_nxt on restart (line 114), increments by 4 and clears bit 1 on an acknowledged fetch (lines 102-103), drives the request address (line 123), and also qualifies low-half buffer writes (line 141). Integrity of request addressing and halfword placement depends on this stored state; availability is the clocked update on restart and acknowledge. The request port is a transport interface, so only the internal setting/store points are listed.

fetch.priv captures ctrl_i.cpu_priv in the restart path (line 115) and is copied to the outgoing request privilege field (line 129). Integrity is established because the request consumer outside this RTL must receive the intended privilege value; the transport output itself is excluded, so the input setting point and stored value are listed.

fetch.state sequences restart/request/pending behavior across lines 92-107 and 116, and its value gates request strobing (line 124), halt reporting (line 145), and prefetch writes (lines 141-142). fetch.restart is sticky across request/pending (lines 91 and 100), clears in the restart state (line 113), forces restart transitions (lines 94 and 104), clears the FIFO sub-units (line 164), and selects issue realignment behavior (lines 205-206). Integrity of request, flush, and progress behavior depends on this control; availability is the defined progression when its gating conditions are met.

The module computes the FIFO write data as two 17-bit entries made from ibus_rsp_i.err and the low/high 16-bit halves of ibus_rsp_i.data (lines 137-138), and computes the lane write-enables so that writes happen only for acknowledged pending responses, with the low half additionally qualified by fetch.pc(1) or not RVC_EN (lines 141-142). These data-and-enable values are delivered into the FIFO sub-units at lines 168-169. Integrity is established because the unseen FIFO consumer must receive exactly the tagged halfwords and admission decision defined by this flow. ibus_rsp_i is a transport port and is therefore not listed.

With RVC_EN, issue.algn is seeded from ctrl_i.pc_nxt(1) on restart (lines 205-206), updated on ctrl_i.if_ack by issue.aset/issue.aclr (lines 207-208), selects which buffered halfword feeds issue.cmd16 (line 195), and steers the comb issue logic (lines 219-248). That logic computes issue.ack as one- or two-lane consumption patterns (lines 223, 228, 238, 243), and ipb.re turns that decision into FIFO read-enables under ctrl_i.if_ack (lines 252-253). With not RVC_EN, issue.algn is tied to 0 and ipb.re derives directly from ctrl_i.if_ack (lines 261 and 266). Integrity is established because instruction order and buffer consumption depend on this state/decision; availability of consumption is conditional on ctrl_i.if_ack.

In RVC_EN builds, the decompressor sub-unit computes issue.cmd32 from issue.cmd16 (lines 188-191), and frontend_o.instr copies issue.cmd32 on compressed-instruction paths (lines 225 and 240). On 32-bit paths, frontend_o.instr is assembled directly from the buffered halfwords (lines 230 and 245), and with not RVC_EN it is always the 32-bit concatenation at line 268. Integrity is established because the next stage must receive exactly the instruction word defined by these branches; availability is conditional on frontend_o.valid.

frontend_o.valid is asserted only when the required buffered halfword(s) are available: compressed paths use one avail bit (lines 222-224 and 237-239), 32-bit paths require both avail bits (lines 229 and 244), and the not-RVC_EN path uses ipb.avail(0) (line 267). Integrity is established because this decision qualifies when frontend_o.instr may be consumed; availability is produced exactly under the RTL-visible buffer-availability conditions.

When RVC_EN is enabled, frontend_o.compr reports whether the selected buffered instruction is treated as compressed or 32-bit, using the selected halfword's low two bits in the issue branches at lines 221-231 and 236-246. When not RVC_EN, the output is tied to '0' at line 269. Integrity is established because this qualifier must match the instruction selection/decompression path used for frontend_o.instr.

frontend_o.fault reports the stored error bit of the selected buffered halfword: ipb.rdata(0)(16) when issue.algn='0' (line 220), ipb.rdata(1)(16) in the other alignment branch (line 235), and ipb.rdata(0)(16) when not RVC_EN (line 270). Integrity is established because this is the module's explicit fault report accompanying the issued instruction.

frontend_o.halted is asserted exactly when the fetch FSM is in request state and the prefetch buffer is not fully free (line 145). Integrity is established because this output is the module's explicit report that a new instruction-bus request is blocked by prefetch-buffer space; availability is produced when that condition holds.
